## Setting Up the Collision Condition

Using 0-indexed positions (0 to 63), Packet $n$ starts at position $n-1$ and moves $n$ ports per minute. At minute $t$, Packet $n$ is at position $(n-1 + nt) \bmod 64$, and Packet 1 is at position $t \bmod 64$.

Packet $n$ ($n \neq 1$) collides with Packet 1 at minute $t$ when:
$$(n-1) + nt \equiv t \pmod{64} \implies (n-1)(t+1) \equiv 0 \pmod{64}$$

Setting $m = n-1 \in \{1,\ldots,63\}$ and $k = t+1$, the condition becomes $m \cdot k \equiv 0 \pmod{64}$.

## Counting Collisions per Minute

Since $64 = 2^6$, the condition $64 \mid mk$ requires $v_2(m) + v_2(k) \geq 6$, where $v_2$ is the 2-adic valuation. For a given $k$ with $v_2(k) = a$, I need $v_2(m) \geq 6-a$, i.e., $m$ divisible by $2^{6-a}$.

The count $f(k)$ of valid $m \in \{1,\ldots,63\}$ is:

| $v_2(k) = a$ | Required divisor | $f(k) = \lfloor 63/2^{6-a}\rfloor$ |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 64 | 0 |
| 1 | 32 | 1 |
| 2 | 16 | 3 |
| 3 | 8 | 7 |
| 4 | 4 | 15 |
| 5 | 2 | 31 |
| $\geq 6$ | 1 | 63 |

## Summing Over Minutes

The total lights lit up to minute $t$ equals $\sum_{k=2}^{t+1} f(k) = \sum_{k=1}^{t+1} f(k)$ (since $f(1)=0$).

**Complete period of 64:** For $k = 1$ to $64$, the $v_2$ distribution gives:
$$0\cdot32 + 1\cdot16 + 3\cdot8 + 7\cdot4 + 15\cdot2 + 31\cdot1 + 63\cdot1 = 192$$

**Finding the target:** $1996 / 192 = 10$ remainder $76$. So 10 complete blocks ($k=1$ to $640$) give $1920$ lights. I need $76$ more from $k=641$ onward.

Since the pattern repeats every 64, $k=641 \equiv 1 \pmod{64}$. Computing the partial sum for $k \equiv 1, 2, \ldots, 31 \pmod{64}$:

$$\underbrace{1+3+1+7+1+3+1}_{k\equiv 2\text{ to }8} + \underbrace{1+3+1+7+1+3+1}_{k\equiv 10\text{ to }16} + \underbrace{1+3+1+7+1+3+1}_{k\equiv 18\text{ to }24} + \underbrace{1+3+1+7+1+3+1}_{k\equiv 26\text{ to }31\text{ (partial)}}$$

Summing all nonzero $f$ values for positions 1–31: $1+3+1+7+1+3+1+15+1+3+1+7+1+3+1 = 49$.

- At $k = 671$ ($\equiv 31$): cumulative $= 1920 + 49 = 1969 < 1996$
- At $k = 672$ ($\equiv 32$): $f(672) = 31$, cumulative $= 1969 + 31 = 2000 \geq 1996$

The 1996th light falls within the batch of 31 lights illuminated at $k = 672$, so $t = 671$.

Packet 1 at minute $t = 671$ is at position $671 \bmod 64$:
$$671 = 10 \times 64 + 31 \implies 671 \bmod 64 = 31$$
